Article Title: PM Modi: I forgive those who abused me & my mother, our job to guide them
Article Text:

Mistakes happen at a young age, says PM Modi

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi said on Friday he will forgive young protesters accused of abusing him and his late mother, saying they are misguided children and it is “our job to show them the right way”.In a video message, Modi said punishing these youth and making them run around courts will not change circumstances, adding that these children have lost their way and must be guided instead of being subjected to any harassment. His comments came amid incidents of criminal cases being lodged against some young protesters for abusing him during the recent student protest. “Everybody saw what happened at Jantar Mantar,” the PM said.They abused not only me but also my late mother. It was such a vile thing. But I want to say today that mistakes happen at a young age, and this is also the opportunity to correct those mistakes,” he said. “I want to forgive them. Society should also accept my decision,” he said in a clear indication that cases against these youngsters will be withdrawn. Modi as Gujarat CM had forgiven a youngster accused of sending a threatening mail to him, sources said.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi said on Friday he will forgive young protesters accused of abusing him and his late mother. He said punishing these youth and making them run around courts will not change circumstances. His comments came amid incidents of criminal cases being lodged against some young protesters for abusing him.

Article Title: ‘How did Hockey India executive board not know?’ Congress questions govt over saffron jersey row
Article Text:
Indian hockey team players in new saffron jersey

Kharge X post

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday sought an explanation from the government and concerned authorities over how the men’s hockey team’s jersey colour was changed from blue to saffron allegedly without the knowledge and approval of the Hockey India executive board.Indian sports teams, including the hockey team, have traditionally worn blue as their primary colour. The decision to change the hockey team’s jersey colour has triggered a major political controversy.The change was announced on July 27, ahead of the World Cup in the Netherlands and Belgium, which begins on August 15.“National symbols, sports, and players should not be used as a medium for narrow-minded political experiments. The government and relevant institutions should immediately reconsider this decision and clarify how such an important decision was taken without the knowledge and consent of Hockey India’s executive board,” Kharge wrote in a post in Hindi on X.He further described the move as not merely a sports-related decision but one “deeply connected” to the sentiments of millions of Indians and the country’s sporting traditions.“Indian players have long been recognised around the world by names such as ‘Men in Blue’, ‘The Blues’, and ‘The Blue Tigers’. This identity is not just about the colour of the jersey, but a legacy of Indian sports. Today, it is difficult to understand why the need was felt to alter this historic identity. The question is not about any particular colour, but about the process of decision-making, transparency, and respect for public sentiments,” the Congress chief said.The veteran politician also pointed out that the colour schemes of both the national tricolour and the Congress flag comprise saffron, white, and green.Alleging the involvement of the RSS in the jersey colour change, Kharge accused the organisation — the ideological mentor of the ruling BJP — of being in a “hurry” to leave its imprint on national symbols and public institutions."It is unfortunate that those whose ideological tradition made no contribution to the freedom movement are now seen in a haste to leave their ideological imprint on every national symbol and every public institution. History knows that the RSS had staunchly opposed the tricolour, and Sardar Patel had even warned them," he added, referring to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the country's first home minister and a Congress stalwart.Hockey India has defended the move, stating that the jersey’s design and colour were intended to “tell a story” and represent “India’s pride”. The federation added that the design was finalised after consultations with players and support staff.However, Hockey India president and former captain Dilip Tirkey claimed that the decision “appeared to have been taken and implemented without being placed before the executive board for discussion and without my prior knowledge.”
Article Summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge seeks an explanation from the government and concerned authorities. The change was announced on July 27, ahead of the World Cup in the Netherlands and Belgium, which begins on August 15. Kharge accused the RSS of being in a “hurry” to leave its imprint on national symbols and public institutions.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Sigmund Freud: 'The more perfect a person is on the outside, the more demons they have on the inside' and why absolute perfection is a facade
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Sigmund Freud

Appearance vs reality

Absolute perfection is a cover-up

Psychological repression

Sigmund Freud was an Austrian neurologist who lived from 1856 to 1939. He is best known as the founding father of psychoanalysis, a clinical method for treating mental health conditions through dialogue between a patient and a psychoanalyst. Freud revolutionized how humanity views the mind by suggesting that much of human behavior is driven by thoughts, desires, and memories locked away in the unconscious mind. Before Freud, mental health was largely viewed through biological or religious lenses. Freud introduced the idea that our internal conflicts, hidden desires, and childhood experiences heavily shape who we are as adults.Most of his quotes entered the academic realm of psychology study and one of them is an observation about appearance and reality. "The more perfect a person is on the outside, the more demons they have on the inside," Freud said.The idea behind the statement that a person who appears perfect on the outside hides demons on the inside ties directly into Freud's theories about how the human mind manages forbidden urges and societal expectations. Freud divided the human psyche into three main parts: the id, the ego, and the superego. The id is the primitive part of our mind that operates purely on instinct, pleasure, and selfish desires.The superego is the exact opposite. It represents our moral conscience, internalized societal rules, ideals, and perfectionism. The ego sits in the middle, trying to balance the wild desires of the id with the strict, moral demands of the superego.When a person tries to project an image of absolute perfection to the world, their superego is working in overdrive. Society rewards people who are polite, composed, highly successful, and morally spotless. To maintain this flawless exterior, a person must constantly suppress any thoughts, feelings, or impulses that society might judge negatively. These suppressed thoughts do not simply vanish. Instead, Freud argued that they get pushed down into the unconscious mind. In this context, the demons refer to these repressed instincts, hidden anger, sexual urges, envy, and unresolved traumas that the person refuses to acknowledge publicly or even to themselves.The core mechanism at work here is psychological repression. Freud believed that repression takes an enormous amount of mental energy. The more energy a person spends trying to look perfect, pristine, and composed, the more pressure builds up inside their unconscious mind. Imagine pushing an inflatable beach ball under the water. The deeper you push it down, and the longer you hold it there, the more force it exerts back against your hands. The surface of the water may look smooth and still, but under the surface, a huge amount of pressure is building up. The demons are not literal evil spirits, but rather those submerged feelings that are desperate to burst back up to the surface.Extreme perfectionism often serves as a defense mechanism. Freud identified several defense mechanisms that the mind uses to protect itself from anxiety. One of these is called reaction formation. Reaction formation happens when a person feels an urge that they consider unacceptable, so they unconsciously act in the exact opposite way to hide it. For instance, someone who struggles with strong feelings of internal chaos, aggression, or self-doubt might overcompensate by becoming obsessed with neatness, strict control, and outward moral purity. The shiny, spotless exterior is actually a protective shield designed to hide the internal turmoil that the person is deeply afraid of facing.This concept also explains why hyper-perfect facades can eventually break down dramatically. Because maintaining a flawless persona requires constant vigilance, the mind eventually tires. When the ego becomes exhausted, the repressed material in the unconscious mind finds sneaky ways to escape. This can show up as sudden emotional outbursts, physical illnesses with no clear medical cause, severe anxiety, or self-destructive behavior that seems to come out of nowhere to outside observers. To the public, it looks like a sudden fall from grace, but from a psychoanalytic perspective, it is simply the long-contained internal pressure finally bursting through the seams of a rigid outward image.Freud’s insight reminds us that genuine human health is not about achieving flawless perfection, but about achieving self-awareness and balance. When people try to disown their darker, flawed, or messy emotions to appear perfect to others, those emotions do not disappear. They grow stronger in the dark corners of the mind. Accepting that human nature is naturally flawed allows people to integrate their shadow side rather than fight it. A person who can acknowledge their weaknesses, mistakes, and complicated feelings does not need to build a fake wall of perfection, and as a result, they carry far fewer hidden demons inside.
Article Summary: Sigmund Freud was an Austrian neurologist who lived from 1856 to 1939. He is best known as the founding father of psychoanalysis. Freud revolutionized how humanity views the mind by suggesting that much of human behavior is driven by thoughts, desires, and memories locked away in the unconscious mind.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Mohammed bin Salman: 'I fear that the day I die, I am going to die without accomplishing what I have in my mind'
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Mohammed bin Salman.

"Because I fear that the day I die, I am going to die without accomplishing what I have in my mind. Life is too short, and a lot of things can happen, and I am really keen to see it with my own eyes, and that is why I am in a hurry."

MBS and a radical departure from traditional Saudi leadership

Philosophy behind the quote

In November 2017, New York Times foreign affairs columnist Thomas L Friedman conducted a landmark interview with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh. During their conversation, Friedman observed the relentless, around-the-clock work culture among the young prince and his senior advisers. Friedman noted that MBS's intense work habits reminded him of a famous line from the musical Hamilton, in which the chorus asks why the protagonist always works like he is "running out of time".When asked directly why he operated at such a breakneck pace, Mohammed bin Salman offered his candid response:Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, widely known as MBS, serves as the Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia . Born in 1985, his rise within the Saudi governance structure was swift. When his father, King Salman bin Abdulaziz, ascended the throne in early 2015, MBS was appointed Minister of Defense. Soon after, he took control of the Council of Economic and Development Affairs (CEDA), giving him direction over the kingdom's economic policy, sovereign wealth fund, and domestic security apparatus.In June 2017, he was formally elevated to Crown Prince.MBS represented a radical departure from traditional Saudi leadership. For decades, the kingdom was led by older monarchs who favored slow, consensus-based, and deeply conservative governance. In contrast, MBS established a centralized, top-down leadership style designed to push rapid economic and cultural changes across the country.While MBS expressed his personal goal and feelings, the quote is a reminder of mortality and human fear of running out of time before what they think needs to be done.When someone says they are in a hurry because life is short and they want to see their ideas become reality, they are dealing with a few basic ideas.First, it is about facing the reality that we all die. Most people try not to think about death, but focusing on the fact that time is limited can act like a wake-up call. It creates a powerful urge to stop waiting around and get things done immediately. The biggest fear here is not death itself, but dying with your work unfinished and your ideas left trapped in your head.Second, it shows a deep desire to turn an inner vision into real-life results. Everyone has ideas, but some people feel an intense personal responsibility to build those ideas into the physical world. They treat life like a race against the clock to prove that their thoughts were not just empty dreams, but something real.Third, it is about wanting to see the results yourself. A lot of people build things for the far future, accepting that they won't be around to see the final product. But this quote pushes back against that idea. It comes from a wish to be alive to witness the change firsthand, rather than leaving it for future generations to enjoy.Finally, it reflects a belief that one person's energy can speed up the world. Instead of letting changes happen slowly over decades, it is the mindset that if you work hard enough and push fast enough, you can force the future to arrive much sooner.
Article Summary: Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, widely known as MBS, serves as the Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia. MBS represented a radical departure from traditional Saudi leadership. The quote is a reminder of mortality and human fear of running out of time before what they think needs to be done.

What Golden State gets in return

Stephen Curry has been a lifelong Warrior but it might be over soon. Curry has spent his entire 17-year career in Golden State, but a new report suggests that could change. Sports Illustrated insider John Karalis says Boston Celtics president Brad Stevens has explored a blockbuster trade for the four-time champion, a move that would come just months after Stevens sent Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia for Paul George and draft capital. With Golden State fading and Boston searching for its next star, the idea has picked up steam even if a deal remains far from close.Stephen Curry's run with the Golden State Warriors may be nearing its end after a report from Sports Illustrated revealed the Boston Celtics have reached out about a blockbuster trade. Insider John Karalis says Celtics president Brad Stevens has been probing Golden State on a deal, just months after trading Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers for Paul George and draft picks.The Warriors have sunk to a 10th-place finish in the West, and if Curry or Golden State lose faith in each other, Boston may find an opening. There is now talk that trade conversations have already begun.At 38, Stephen Curry remains one of the league's best guards, averaging 26.6 points, 3.6 rebounds and 4.7 assists per game last season while shooting 46.8% from the field and 39.3% from three. But the roster around him has crumbled.Jimmy Butler is still working back from a torn ACL, and Golden State leaned so hard on aging veterans that it finished 10th in the West.That decline is why speculation has crept in for the first time in the Curry era. Karalis pointed to "a crack in the foundation of the Curry-era Warriors," the first real crack of its kind since Curry arrived in the Bay Area.Boston is short a star after shipping Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia for Paul George and future picks, a swap that left much of the fan base unimpressed. Bringing in Curry alongside Jayson Tatum would give Stevens the kind of splash move that could win those fans back and put the Celtics right back into title contention.Golden State's side of the equation is different. The Warriors are not built to compete now, and if Curry or the front office start to sense that reality, moving on while his value is still high becomes a real option, even if unlikely today.Brad Stevens has already been on the phone with the Warriors brass to pitch a deal.Adding Curry gives Boston a second superstar alongside Jayson Tatum and instantly restores the Celtics as a threat in the East, even after a summer that left fans questioning the front office's direction. His shooting gravity alone would open up the floor in ways the current roster cannot match.Parting with Paul George, Sam Hauser and draft capital would sting, but Boston still holds multiple first-round picks even after this package, leaving Stevens room to keep building around his two stars.Paul George gives the Warriors a proven wing scorer to pair with their remaining pieces, even as he arrives with an uncertain long-term fit at this stage of his career. Sam Hauser adds shooting depth off the bench.The real value for Golden State would be the draft picks, giving a team that finished 10th in the West a path to restock through the draft rather than continuing to patch the roster with aging veterans.Curry, even at 38, would immediately elevate Boston's ceiling in a way Paul George, Sam Hauser and a handful of picks likely wouldn't for Golden State. It's a fair value swap on paper, but the star power tilts this toward the Celtics if it ever actually happens.
Article Summary: Stephen Curry has spent his entire 17-year career in Golden State, but a new report suggests that could change. Sports Illustrated insider John Karalis says Boston Celtics president Brad Stevens has explored a blockbuster trade for the four-time champion. The Warriors have sunk to a 10th-place finish in the West, and if Curry or Golden State lose faith in each other, Boston may find an opening.

Article Title: Why Pat Freiermuth’s split-second reaction during a chaotic Steelers camp fight has fans calling him a true hero?
Article Text:
Pat Freiermuth reaches over the barricade to pull a young fan away from a fight during Pittsburgh Steelers training camp, earning praise for his quick reaction and awareness(Getty)

Pat Freiermuth’s quick reaction protected a young fan during Pittsburgh Steelers training camp chaos

Pat Freiermuth created a memorable moment at Pittsburgh Steelers training camp, but it had nothing to do with a catch or a touchdown. During an autograph session near the practice field, a fight broke out among fans, and the Steelers tight end quickly stepped in when he noticed a young child standing close to the disturbance.A video from the incident shows several adults pushing and throwing punches as people nearby try to move away. Amid the confusion, Freiermuth reached over the barricade and pulled the child away from the crowd, helping the youngster avoid the dangerous situation.The incident happened during Day 4 of Steelers training camp when an autograph session became tense. According to the person who shared the footage on social media, the disagreement started among fans trying to get player signatures before turning into a physical confrontation.The fight quickly attracted attention as several people moved away from the area. However, Freiermuth’s focus went toward the child who was standing near the altercation. The Steelers tight end reacted instantly, reaching over the barrier and moving the youngster away from the crowd.The chaos was broken up soon after, and no major injuries were reported. While the altercation itself grabbed attention, fans across social media focused on Freiermuth’s reaction.Many praised him for noticing the child’s position and acting before the situation could become more serious.A fan wrote on X, “Thankfully the Steelers player pulled that kid out of the way,” highlighting how Freiermuth protected the young fan when the crowd became unpredictable.Another fan added, “Respect to Pat for taking that little kid so he doesn’t get hurt,” praising the tight end for putting someone else’s safety ahead of everything else.One more fan shared an emotional reaction to the moment, writing, “Muuuuuuuuuuuth with the grab to save the kid,” as many Steelers supporters celebrated the tight end’s awareness and quick response.Another fan added, “In all my years going to LaTrobe I have never seen that.”Some fans credited Mike Tomlin for this class act and said, “The Tomlin effect 👀”Another fan said, It's Pittsburgh...on brand. Why do you still have this Twitter? It was supposed to be DELETED LAST DECEMBER WHEN THE BROWNS BEAT THE STEELERS.The reaction from fans showed why the moment stood out. Training camp is usually a place where families gather to watch players, collect autographs, and enjoy the experience around the team. A sudden fight changed the atmosphere, but Freiermuth’s response gave fans something positive to remember.The Pittsburgh Steelers tight end has already drawn attention during camp for his performance on the field. After a challenging 2025 season, expectations are high for Freiermuth to play a bigger role in the offense, especially after the team did not make a major move at tight end following Jonnu Smith’s departure.However, this moment showed a different side of the veteran player. It was not about statistics, targets, or touchdowns. It was about awareness and making the right decision when someone needed help.Freiermuth’s action lasted only a few seconds, but it left a lasting impression. In a chaotic moment at Steelers training camp, he made sure a young fan moved away from danger, and that is why fans are celebrating him beyond the football field.
Article Summary: Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth pulled a young fan away from a fight during training camp. The incident happened during an autograph session when a fight broke out among fans. Fans praised the tight end for his quick reaction and awareness.

Article Title: Brock Lesnar declares future in WWE after Hell in a Cell loss to Oba Femi at SummerSlam
Article Text:
Oba Femi defeats Brock Lesnar. Image via: Rich Freeda/ WWE via Getty Images

Oba Femi defeats Brock Lesnar at SummerSlam

Brock Lesnar crowns Oba Femi as WWE's future

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brock Lesnar to be inducted into the Minnesota M Club Hall of Fame

Brock Lesnar's future in WWE took a symbolic turn at SummerSlam Night 1, where Oba Femi beat him inside Hell in a Cell to win their trilogy 2-1 and hand Lesnar his first-ever loss in the structure. The result came Saturday at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, closing out a rivalry that began at WrestleMania 42.Moments after the bell, Lesnar grabbed a microphone and told the crowd he represents the past while Femi represents WWE's future, a rare public passing-of-the-torch moment that raised immediate questions about what comes next for The Beast Incarnate.Oba Femi beat Brock Lesnar inside Hell in a Cell at SummerSlam Night 1, closing out their three-match rivalry with a second win over The Beast Incarnate in Minneapolis. The finish came when Femi punched a steel chair out of Lesnar's hands and connected with the Fall From Grace, ending a war that had already spilled through a table, steel steps, and the exposed wood beneath the ring canvas.Lesnar opened with three German suplexes before Femi shrugged them off and tossed him outside, driving Lesnar shoulder-first into the ring steps. Lesnar answered back with steel chair shots and more suplexes, eventually tearing up the mat to expose the boards underneath and hitting a Tombstone Piledriver on the bare wood.Femi kicked out. Three F5s followed, and Femi kicked out of those too before turning the momentum for good.The loss marked the first time Lesnar had ever lost inside Hell in a Cell, a structure where he'd gone 2-0 before Saturday.The two embraced after the bell, and Lesnar called for a microphone. He told the Minneapolis crowd that he represents WWE's past and Femi represents its future, a symbolic handoff that closes out a rivalry stretching back to WrestleMania 42, where Femi's win prompted an apparent Lesnar retirement.Lesnar didn't stay retired long. He attacked Femi on Raw weeks later, then beat him in a controversial decision at WWE Clash in Italy to force the rubber match. Femi, fresh off winning the 2026 King of the Ring, gave up an earned title opportunity to instead settle things with Lesnar inside the Cell, a decision that paid off with Saturday's win.Away from SummerSlam, the University of Minnesota announced Lesnar as part of its 2026 M Club Hall of Fame class, with induction set for Oct. 2 at Huntington Bank Stadium.Lesnar wrestled at Minnesota from 1998 to 2000, going 55-3 with 23 pins and winning the 2000 NCAA heavyweight title after finishing as runner-up the year before. He'll be honored at the Gophers' Oct. 3 football game against Michigan, closing out a fall that already saw him hand the WWE torch to Oba Femi in the ring he once dominated as an amateur star just miles from campus.
Article Summary: Oba Femi beat Brock Lesnar inside Hell in a Cell to win their trilogy 2-1. Lesnar told the crowd he represents the past while Femi represents WWE's future. The University of Minnesota announced Lesnar as part of its 2026 M Club Hall of Fame class.

Former basketball player Troy Payne shared videos from the ceremony on his Instagram Story, while Complex Sports also reported the wedding on Instagram. Neither Mitchell nor Jones has publicly confirmed the marriage, but the videos quickly drew attention from fans celebrating the couple's latest chapter.The reported wedding comes just over a year after the Cleveland Cavaliers star and the Grammy-winning artist announced their engagement. Their relationship has largely stayed out of the spotlight, making the emergence of wedding footage a rare glimpse into one of sports and music's most private power couples.While Mitchell and Jones have yet to share the news themselves, the videos posted by Payne offered fans their first look at what appeared to be the couple's wedding day. Representatives for the couple previously revealed they got engaged while on vacation after a busy stretch that included Mitchell's NBA season and Jones' sold-out tour.Jones has often spoken about the significance of their relationship. Article Title: His grandfather paid $2,200 for an Allis-Chalmers tractor in 1953; 62 years later, Kevin Klahn bought it back and restored it
Article Text:
Representative Image (Image Credit: Wikipedia)

A machine that built memories

(Image Credit: Farm Progress/ Harlen Persinger)

A decades-long journey home

Preserving more than metal

A tractor that once powered a family farm has come full circle after more than six decades. According to an exclusive report by Farm Progress, Kevin Klahn, the grandson of the farmer who bought the Allis-Chalmers WD new for $2,200 in 1953, tracked down the very same tractor, purchased it back in 2015 (62 years later), and painstakingly restored it to its former glory. More than a vintage machinery project, the restoration became a heartfelt tribute to his family's farming legacy.When Kevin Klahn's grandfather bought the Allis-Chalmers WD in 1953, it was an important investment for the family farm. The tractor became an important part of the family's farming history after it was purchased in 1953.The tractor was eventually sold and passed through several owners over the years. Yet for Klahn, the tractor was never just another piece of equipment; it represented a connection to the generations before him.Determined to reclaim a piece of his family's history, Klahn began searching for the tractor decades after it had left the farm. His efforts eventually paid off when he located the original Allis-Chalmers WD that his grandfather had purchased more than 60 years earlier.In 2015, exactly 62 years after the original purchase, Klahn bought the tractor back.Although time had left its mark, he saw its potential, not merely as a collectible antique but as a family heirloom worth preserving.The rediscovered tractor became the centrepiece of a meticulous restoration project. Klahn carefully restored the tractor, aiming to preserve the historic machine's original character.Restoring a 70-year-old tractor demanded patience, craftsmanship and countless hours of work. But for Klahn, the effort was never solely about fresh paint or mechanical perfection. It was about honouring the generations who had relied on the tractor and ensuring their story would continue to be told. Today, the gleaming Allis-Chalmers WD stands as both a beautifully restored classic and a symbol of family heritage. It reflects a growing appreciation among vintage tractor enthusiasts for preserving the stories behind historic farm equipment rather than simply restoring old machines.For many farming families, tractors are more than tools, they are silent witnesses to decades of hard work, changing seasons and shared memories. Klahn's restoration captures that sentiment perfectly. Instead of remaining a forgotten relic scattered across different owners, the tractor has returned to where its story began. More than 70 years after rolling onto the family farm for the first time, it once again represents the values of dedication, craftsmanship and the enduring bond between generations. Sometimes, the greatest restoration is not simply bringing an old machine back to life, it is bringing a family's history home.

Article Title: 18 years after Saina Nehwal, Tanvi Sharma brings Taipei Open title back to India
Article Text:
Tanvi Sharma (Image credit: BAI)

Dominant display in the final



Emotional moment with coach

Another milestone for the teenage star



Indian badminton player Tanvi Sharma won the first BWF World Tour title of her career after beating Vietnam's Thuy Linh Nguyen in the women's singles final of the Taipei Open Super 300 on Sunday.The 17-year-old from Punjab defeated the sixth seed 21-16, 21-16 in just 36 minutes to lift her maiden Super 300 trophy.Tanvi, who is coached by Park Tae-sang, the former coach of PV Sindhu, also became the first Indian woman to win the Taipei Open singles title since Saina Nehwal in 2008.Tanvi made an excellent start and used her clever drop shots and deceptive strokes to trouble Nguyen. She quickly raced to a 10-2 lead in the opening game.Although a few unforced errors allowed the Vietnamese player to reduce the gap, Tanvi regained control after the mid-game break. Strong smashes from both sides of the court helped her seal the first game 21-16.Nguyen started the second game better and moved 3-0 ahead, but Tanvi fought back to level the score at 3-3. She once again mixed powerful smashes with delicate net shots to take control of the rallies.The Indian gradually increased her lead to 15-10 and then 18-12.She earned seven match points and, despite missing three of them, finished the match with another winner to claim the biggest title of her career.After winning the title, Tanvi celebrated by taking off her gold medal and placing it around the neck of her coach Park Tae-sang. The two then posed together for photographs in a heartwarming moment.At 17 years and 222 days, Tanvi became the youngest finalist in the history of the Taipei Open, breaking the previous record held by Korean doubles legend Lee Yong Dae, who reached the men's doubles final in 2006 at 17 years and 287 days.Tanvi has enjoyed a rapid rise over the last two years. She became the first Indian to win two medals at a single World Junior Championships, claiming silver in girls' singles and bronze in the mixed team event.She was also part of the Indian team that won the country's first-ever gold medal at the Asian Team Championships.A former world junior No. 1, Tanvi had finished runner-up at the 2025 US Open Super 300, as well as the Odisha Masters Super 100 and Guwahati Masters Super 100, before finally winning her maiden BWF World Tour title in Taipei.
Article Summary: Tanvi Sharma beat Vietnam's Thuy Linh Nguyen in the women's singles final of the Taipei Open Super 300 on Sunday. Article Title: Draw inspiration from Tilak’s life to contribute for nation-building, Shah tells youth
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah confers Lokmanya Tilak National Award on NSA Ajit Doval in the presence of chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, and deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar, in Pune on Saturday

Pune:

Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday urged the country’s youth to draw inspiration from freedom fighter Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak’s life to contribute for nation-building.Calling Lokmanya Tilak the tallest figure in the freedom struggle movement, Shah said, “Along with the freedom struggle movement, Tilak stressed on achieving self-reliance, discipline and sense of responsibility towards the nation. The younger generation should follow the life of Lokmanya Tilak to draw inspiration and contribute towards nation-building.”Shah on Saturday gave away the Lokmanya Tilak National Award to national security adviser (NSA) Ajit Doval at a ceremony in Pune. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , both the deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar, president of Lokmanya Tilak Smarak Trust Rohit Tilak and others attended the award ceremony.Mentioning Tilak’s literary work of “Gita Rahasya”, Shah said, “Tilak’s literature will never be outdated. It remains eternal. If the youth of the country read Gita through Tilak’s point of view, they will never commit any mistake.”Congratulating Doval on receiving the Tilak national award, Shah said the first appointment Narendra Modi made after becoming the Prime Minister in 2014 was that of Doval as the NSA. “Under PM Modi’s leadership, India’s defence and foreign policies were strengthened, and Doval played an important role in shaping these policies.Doval is India’s longest serving NSA. The internal and external security of the country transformed under his tenure,” Shah said.“The Multi Agency Centre (MAC) has become the backbone of the country’s internal security under the Modi-led government and the strong foundation of MAC was laid by Doval as its founding chairman. When the history of Modi’s tenure would be written and an assessment would be made of the country’s internal and external security, a golden page about Doval would be included in it,” Shah said.Doval in his speech urged the country’s youth to sacrifice their personal interest and devote life to nation building. “We have got the window of opportunity to contribute to build the nation, which today’s youth should not let go. Remembering the sacrifices of our freedom fighters in the country’s freedom movement, the youth of the country should also dedicate their life to take the nation to new heights,” he said.Cautioning the youth regarding the challenges before the country, Doval said, “While India is on a path of development, not all are happy with our progress. Some people and countries are threatened by India’s development. Some internal and external challenges still persist before the country. The young generation should stand up to take on those challenges.”Doval said the country’s growth had been expedited under the leadership of PM Modi and home minister Shah, who never showed any hesitation in taking some tough decisions in the interest of the country. “India still has not reached its goal but we are fortunate to have a strong leadership of Modi and Shah, who ensured that people of the country get a conducive atmosphere to achieve its goal,” Doval added.Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said the combination of Modi, Shah’s leadership and Doval’s expertise in national security had transformed India’s image as a stronger nation in the entire world. He said, “Due to the efforts of Modi, Shah and Doval, we have sent a strong message to the entire world that India cannot be bullied anymore and in case of any threat, we can proactively respond by entering into the enemy’s territory also. ”Shah also paid floral tributes to the statue of Annabhau Sathe near Sarasbaug.
Article Summary: Amit Shah on Saturday gave away the Lokmanya Tilak National Award to national security adviser (NSA) Ajit Doval at a ceremony in Pune. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar also attended the award ceremony.

Article Title: 'I have a lot of respect for her': Pakistan's first female CWG boxing medallist credits Mary Kom for inspiring her
Article Text:
Mary Kom

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Growing up in Pakistan's Punjab province, Fatima Zahra had few female boxing role models in her own country. She found one across the border in India's MC Mary Kom, whose journey inspired her to take up the sport and eventually become Pakistan's first female Commonwealth Games boxing medallist.The 22-year-old from Sargodha in Pakistan's Punjab province won a bronze medal in the women's 60kg event at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, becoming the first Pakistani woman boxer to stand on a Commonwealth Games podium.After her medal-winning campaign, Fatima said the person who inspired her to take up boxing was India's six-time world champion Mary Kom "I am inspired by India's Mary Kom," Fatima told news agency PTI after securing her bronze medal.Born into a poor farming family, Mary Kom overcame financial hardship, social resistance and limited resources to become one of the most successful boxers in history. She secretly trained in her early years while helping her family in the fields before winning six world championship titles, an Olympic bronze medal, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games gold medals, and five Asian Championships.Fatima said the 2014 Bollywood film based on Mary Kom's life became a source of motivation when she started boxing."I used to watch the film made on her life. When I started boxing I used to watch that movie and train. I have a lot of respect for her and inshallah one day I will become like her. I hope I can meet her," Fatima said.Like Mary Kom, Fatima also had to overcome opposition from her family before she could continue with boxing."My background is not that strong. My basic coach taught me everything," she said, as quotes by PTI."My family was against boxing. They would not let me go for training but I fought with them and continued training."She said her family's attitude has changed completely over the years."And now they are more tense than me for my fight and competition," she said with a smile.Fatima hopes her medal will encourage more girls in Pakistan to take up sport and follow their dreams."I was also just another girl. I joined boxing, trained and worked hard. I want other girls who are told to work at home to come out like me."
Article Summary: Fatima Zahra is Pakistan's first female Commonwealth Games boxing medallist. The 22-year-old won a bronze medal in the women's 60kg event in Glasgow. Fatima said the person who inspired her to take up boxing was India's Mary Kom.

Article Title: Fallout in West Indies camp? Alzarri Joseph hits back at Daren Sammy over 'declined selection' claim
Article Text:
Alzarri Joseph and Daren Sammy (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

West Indies fast bowler Alzarri Joseph has responded to head coach Daren Sammy's comments regarding his absence from the ongoing home Test series against Pakistan, insisting that the public narrative surrounding his decision lacked important context.When Cricket West Indies announced the squad for the two-match series, the board stated that Joseph would miss the matches due to personal reasons. However, Sammy later told reporters that the pacer had been selected but chose not to accept the call-up, saying Joseph had "declined selection."Speaking on the Antigua Observer's Good Morning Jojo Sports Show, Joseph said Sammy's remarks created an unnecessary perception about his commitment to the team."We had a chat, myself and the head coach. I've also had a chat with CWI, and if you realise the statement CWI released said personal reasons. Mr Sammy, being around for a long time, he knows exactly what that statement would have done so, to be honest, I have nothing to say to Mr Sammy in terms of his statement," Joseph said."As I said, he knows exactly what that statement would have done and the narrative it would have pushed in the public.Obviously, I've been out for an entire year. I haven't played at international intensity for so long after having a second stress fracture," Joseph added.The 29-year-old explained that his decision was influenced by concerns over his physical condition after recently returning from a lengthy injury layoff.“We spoke about me playing the two Test matches here, playing five back-to-back ODIs [against New Zealand earlier this month], and how my body was feeling, and I knew to myself, my body was not ready to go into another Test series. So, the statement in itself is controversial, without context,” he said.Joseph spent close to a year on the sidelines after suffering a second stress fracture in his lower back, an injury that ruled him out of the West Indies' tours of India and New Zealand. He only returned to international cricket during the Test series against Sri Lanka earlier this year.Having only recently resumed playing at the highest level, the right-arm quick said he wanted to carefully manage his workload to avoid another setback.The contrasting explanations from Joseph and Sammy have also sparked discussion over the state of their relationship. The fast bowler, however, insisted that personal equations would not affect his commitment to representing the West Indies."I'm a professional, so I'm going to go to work. I am representing the West Indies. I'm not representing Daren Sammy, so for me, I'm neither here nor there in terms of a relationship," Joseph said.“I don't go there to make friends. I go there to work and do a job and represent the people of the West Indies,” he added.
Article Summary: West Indies fast bowler Alzarri Joseph has responded to head coach Daren Sammy's comments regarding his absence from the Test series against Pakistan. Joseph said Sammy's remarks created an unnecessary perception about his commitment to the team. The 29-year-old explained that his decision was influenced by concerns over his physical condition after recently returning from a lengthy injury layoff.

Article Title: A love that waited 7 years ended in 1 month: Army major returns home draped in Tricolour
Article Text:
Major Hamza Arif had married his Hindu engineer partner just one month prior





JAISALMER: What was meant to be the beginning of a lifetime together turned into an unimaginable tragedy for Major Hamza Arif and his young bride.After spending seven years in a committed relationship and finally convincing their families to accept their marriage, the couple had tied the knot only a month ago.Before the henna on his wife's hands had even faded, fate dealt a devastating blow.Late on Thursday night, Major Hamza Arif lost his life in a horrific road accident near Jaisalmer Military Station when the Tata Safari SUV he was driving collided with a camel and overturned several times.With his death, the dreams and hopes his wife had cherished for their new life together were shattered forever.The couple had recently begun their married life with great optimism.Major Hamza had purchased a new Tata Safari SUV, and his family in Indore had already begun preparations for a grand wedding reception planned for December, when the newlyweds were expected to visit home. Instead of returning to celebrate, the young Army officer is now making his final journey wrapped in the Indian Tricolour.Photographs from the couple's wedding have gone viral on social media, capturing moments of joy, hope and togetherness.The images have deeply moved people, highlighting the heartbreaking contrast between their recent happiness and the tragedy that followed.Major Hamza Arif is survived by his parents and three sisters.He was the only son of a middle-class Bohra Muslim family, and his untimely death has left the family devastated.According to his childhood friend Aman Shukla of Indore, Major Hamza was a native of Dhanvantri Nagar, Indore.He completed his Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering from Chameli Devi College in 2016.Determined to serve the nation, he cleared the selection process and joined the Indian Army in 2017.Through dedication, discipline and exceptional service, he earned three promotions within just nine years, rising to the rank of Major. He was serving at Jaisalmer Military Station at the time of the accident.The fatal crash occurred around 12:30am on Thursday night, nearly 8 kilometres from Jaisalmer city, when the SUV suddenly struck a camel on the road inside the Army area.The impact was so severe that the vehicle overturned four to five times, leaving Major Hamza critically injured.Two other officers travelling with him, Lieutenant Ayushman Gusain and Lieutenant Abhinav Rathore, also sustained injuries.All three were rushed to the Army Hospital, where doctors declared Major Hamza dead. The two injured officers continue to receive treatment.Another childhood friend, Navneet Hardia, said the tragedy has left everyone in shock, noting that Major Hamza had only recently married his longtime partner, an engineer from a Hindu family, after a seven-year relationship.The couple had faced considerable challenges in persuading their families to accept their union before finally solemnising their marriage through a court marriage just a month ago."The family had been eagerly waiting for the couple to come home in December and had already started planning a grand reception," he said. "No one could have imagined that instead of welcoming the newlyweds, they would be receiving Hamza's mortal remains wrapped in the national flag."Friends said Major Hamza's wife had looked forward to building a happy life with her husband and supporting him through his Army career. Those dreams have now been cruelly cut short. Overwhelmed with grief, she is accompanying his mortal remains to Indore for his final journey.Major Hamza had recently purchased the Tata Safari SUV involved in the accident and was driving it himself when the tragedy occurred.The accident has plunged Jaisalmer Military Station and Indore into mourning. Fellow officers, soldiers, friends and relatives have remembered Major Hamza as a dedicated Army officer, a compassionate human being and a humble individual who was deeply respected by everyone who knew him.According to family members and local representatives, Major Hamza Arif's mortal remains will be brought to Indore on Saturday, where he will be laid to rest with full military honours in accordance with the traditions of the Indian Army and the religious customs of the Bohra Muslim community.His passing has left behind not only a grieving family but also a young bride whose dreams of a lifetime together were tragically cut short just weeks after their marriage.
Article Summary: Major Hamza Arif lost his life in a horrific road accident near Jaisalmer Military Station. The Tata Safari SUV he was driving collided with a camel and overturned several times. Major Hamza had married his Hindu engineer partner just one month prior to the tragedy. The young Army officer is now making his final journey wrapped in the Indian Tricolour.

Article Title: 'You are a fool to live so openly, Mallya told Nirav before his arrest'

To avoid being seen in restaurants, he would pay private chefs £200 to £300 per hour to come to his apartment and cook, but they were never of Indian origin, and it was never the same chef twice, the podcast revealed."I don't think he was clever enough to come up with the (Punjab National Bank) scam himself," the source added. The podcast speculates that Nirav has submitted a second asylum case, which is why he has not gone back. Nirav's solicitor Anand Doobay, who Mallya also used, told TOI: "We are not commenting."

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.

Article Title: 4 held for theft of 17 kg silver mask, cladding of Shivling at historic temple in Maharashtra's Khopoli
Article Text:
Khopoli police arrested four burglars for stealing silver items from a historic temple





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khopoli police in Raigad detected the burglary at the 18th century historic Shree Vireshwar temple, where 17 kg silver mask and silver cladding on Shivling was stolen on July 19 past midnight around 2 am, by arresting four accused burglars on Tuesday.The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe (36) and Vikas Agiwale (25), who were arrested from Shirur, Pune district and Dilip Jadhav (40) and Sakharam Gaikwad (40), who were arrested from Parner in Ahilyanagar district.The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust from the donations received from devotees.Sachin Hire, senior inspector of Khopoli said, "On July 19, the assistant priest at the temple identified as Kishore Shigwan (56) lodge a complaint that the silver mask and cladding on Shivling was stolen. The thieves had entered the temple by breaking the chain and lock of the rear gate, which always remained close as the devotees were allowed entry only from the front gate.""Upon checking CCTV camera footage at the temple, it was seen that four masked men had entered the sanctum sanctorum around 2 am and decamped with the silver mask and cladding on the Shivling. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under BNS sections for house tres-pass, theft in a dwelling house and joint criminal liability. "Inspector Hire said, "Multiple teams were formed to trace the gang of burglars.Using technical expertise and informer network, we zeroed-in on four history-sheeters. They were traced to Pune and Ahilyanagar district and gradually apprehended on Tuesday.""They have revealed the place where they have hidden the stolen silver mask and cladding. Accordingly, a police team will recover the stolen valuables. Previously, there are criminal cases of theft and robbery registered against the arrested accused in Ahilyanagar and Pune districts."
Article Summary: The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust. The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe, Vikas Agiwale, Dilip Jadhav and Sakharam Gaikwad.

The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters.Gajanan Kadam, senior inspector of AHTU said, "As per the information received about prostitution being carried out at Hotel Abode Inn Lodging and Boarding in Taloja, we set a trap by sending a decoy customer, whom the lodge manager provided a woman for sexual favour for Rs 3,000 that was accepted by one waiter. On the signal of the customer customer, we raided the lodge, where 9 women were kept for prostitution. Article Title: Truck driver arrested from Gujarat for killing fellow driver with iron rod over caste dispute in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Taloja police have caught a truck driver involved in the tragic murder of a fellow driver during a dispute fueled by caste discrimination (Representative image)

NAVI MUMBAI: Taloja police have arrested a 40-year-old truck driver who had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod in the truck parking lot of Nisha Transport company in Nitlas village near Taloja industrial area in Panvel taluka on July 14 early morning.The accused was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday, while he was escaping by train to his home town in UP.The arrested accused has been identified as Ramesh Kumar Yadav and the murder victim as Chandan Pandey, both hailing from UP.Sagar Nikam, PI (crime) of Taloja said, "The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP. The accused Yadav had fatally assaulted the victim Pandey as the latter being a Brahmin used to humiliate Yadav from OBC by treating him as inferior, as claimed by the accused Yadav."PI Nikam informed, "On Monday night, an argument has ensued between Pandey and Yadav in the parking lot over caste discrimination. As they quarrelled, the other truck drivers intervened and resolved the matter. On Tuesday around 5.30 am, again both of them quarrelled, when Yadav assaulted on Pandey's head with an iron rod that proved fatal.""Pandey escaped after threatening other truckers if they attempted to catch him. The security guard Mohammad Alam Hajif-ul Khan (58) informed the police. Pandey was rushed to Panvel sub-district hospital where he was declared brought dead. Subsequently, a murder case was registered against the accused Yadav. His photograph found in his parked truck was immediately circulated to the GRP and RPF at railway stations where multiple trains heading to UP halt.""On Friday, the Valsad GRP informed us that Yadav has been detained at Valsad railway station while he was travelling in an express train to escape to his hometown in UP. Our police team reached Valsad and arrested Yadav. The Panvel JMFC court has remanded Yadav to police custody untill July 21."
Article Summary: Ramesh Kumar Yadav, 40, was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday. He had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod. The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP.

Article Title: Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi
Article Text:
Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi (Representational Image)

NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai crime branch unit-2 team has arrested a murder accused from Bhiwandi while conducting a parallel probe in the murder case registered at NRI Coastal police station on Friday after an unidentified man's body with head injuries was found on the pavement near D-Mart in sector 15, Belapur on Friday around 1 am.The arrested accused has been identified as Mohammad Irfan Mohammed Husain Ansari (36) and the murder victim as Salman Anwar Shaikh (27), a resident of Govandi. Both working as rag pickers for livelihood.Anil Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-2 informed that, during the probe, when inquired with some rag pickers in the locality, we got an eye witness, who knew Ansari and had seen him assaulting Shaikh with a wooden stick on Thursday night as a quarrel broke out between them after they together consumed liquor near the pavement.The eye witness told that Ansari would pick up rags during day and would spend night where ever he found empty gala or incomplete under construction bldg in Belapur and his father resided in Bhiwandi.Using technical expertise and informer network Ansari was apprehended from Bhiwandi within 24 hours. Thereafter, the murder victim's identity was revealed by him.SPI Patil said, "Ansari claimed that Shaikh was habitual of abusing others after getting drunk. On Thursday night, after the liquor session, Shaikh turned violent without being provoked and attempted to assault him with an iron rod after pushing him to the ground. Hence, he confronted Shaikh by assaulting him with a wooden stick on his head. Seeing Shaikh bleeding profusely and fallen unconscious, he escaped to Bhiwandi. "
Article Summary: Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi. Mohammad Irfan Mohammed Husain Ansari (36) and the murder victim as Salman Anwar Shaikh (27), a resident of Govandi. Both working as rag pickers for livelihood.

Article Title: SIR extension? Teachers fear academics will suffer
Article Text:
BLOs visit a shop during SIR drive in Khadki

Pune:





After Odisha and Telangana received extensions for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, there is growing speculation that Maharashtra too could seek more time if the exercise is not completed by the Aug 8 deadline.But for thousands of teachers doubling up as booth-level officers (BLOs), an extension offers little comfort. Many said they would rather see the exercise conclude on schedule or have teachers handling higher classes exempted from election duty as the dual responsibility of teaching and voter verification is beginning to affect classroom teaching.Teachers deployed as BLOs told TOI that their workday now stretches well into the night. After teaching through the day, they spend the rest of it and a good part of the evening visiting households, attending SIR camps and making repeated phone calls to voters who could not be contacted during door-to-door verification.“We finish classes in the afternoon and head straight for election duty. If residents are unavailable, we sit at camps and make calls, asking them to bring their forms. Many never turn up, so we have to follow up again the next day,” a govt school teacher serving as a BLO in Pune.Other educators said urban constituencies have made the exercise particularly challenging because of frequent migration, rented accommodation and outdated electoral records.“In many cases, voters have shifted from one assembly constituency to another but their names are at the old address. Sometimes, the address is incomplete or the family has moved out. We spend hours searching for a voter only to find no one lives there anymore,” another teacher-BLO said.Several teachers said verification camps are a practical necessity. “We do visit homes. Only after finding houses locked repeatedly do we call voters or send WhatsApp messages asking them to visit the camp. Many cooperate, but others don’t answer calls or fail to turn up even after confirming. We then have to repeat the process,” another BLO said.Election officials said they have received repeated representations from teachers seeking relief from BLO duties because of the growing academic workload.“Teachers want to be excused from election duty, particularly those handling Stds X and XII. They say they have to complete the syllabus, conduct practicals, unit tests and hold extra classes for board students. However, the SIR is a statutory exercise and the available manpower has to be deployed to complete it within the prescribed timeline,” an election official said.Teachers said the pressure of balancing both responsibilities was becoming increasingly difficult. “We are already conducting extra classes to compensate for teaching hours lost to election work. Lesson planning, assessments and remedial teaching have all been affected,” a secondary school teacher from Pune said.Another teacher said students appearing for board examinations need sustained academic support. “If teachers of higher classes could be spared from BLO work, schools would be able to manage both responsibilities much better,” the teacher added.Some teachers said repeated interactions with voters also added to the pressure. “Most cooperate, but others don’t understand the SIR drive and scold us. We still follow up because every voter has to be contacted,” a BLO said.
Article Summary: Odisha and Telangana received extensions for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. There is growing speculation that Maharashtra too could seek more time if the exercise is not completed by the Aug 8 deadline. Thousands of teachers doubling up as booth-level officers (BLOs) say they would rather see the exercise conclude on schedule.

Article Title: Whistling, pulling hand of girl not sexual harassment: Madras HC
Article Text:
The Madras High Court has suspended a three-year sentence for a man. He was convicted under the Pocso Act for his actions (Representative image)





CHENNAI: Whistling at a minor girl and pulling her hand when she did not respond is not sexual harassment, Madras high court has said. “Such act cannot be straightaway termed as sexual intent. At the most, it can be termed as harassment and not an act of sexual assault,” the court added.Justice M Nirmal Kumar made the observation while suspending a three-year sentence ordered against a man by a special court under the Pocso Act . The sentence was suspended till the disposal of the appeal moved by the man challenging the trial court order.“The overt act attributed against the petitioner is that while standing on the balcony, he whistled and called the victim. Since the victim did not respond, the petitioner came down and pulled her by hand. Thereafter, the victim pulled herself out from him and informed her mother the same. From the statements of witnesses and materials available on record, it is seen that the petitioner pulled the victim by hand, when the victim failed to respond to his whistle,” the court said.Such an act cannot be straightaway termed as sexual intent and at most, it can be termed as harassment and not an act of sexual assault.Hence, the judgment needs to be re-considered, the court said.“Considering the fact that there are arguable points involved in this appeal and it would take some time for the appeal to be taken up for final hearing, this court is inclined to suspend the sentence imposed on the petitioner.”According to the petitioner, there was a fight between the petitioner and the victim’s father, and there was an exchange of blows. Taking advantage of the minority of the girl, the victim’s parents projected a false case as though the petitioner called the victim and sexually assaulted her.
Article Summary: Madras High Court has suspended a three-year sentence for a man. He was convicted under the Pocso Act for his actions. “Such act cannot be straightaway termed as sexual intent. At the most, it can be termed as harassment and not an act of sexual assault,” the court added.

Article Title: Hundreds celebrate healing at cancer survivors’ reunion
Article Text: Chennai: Hundreds of cancer survivors gathered at Adyar Cancer Institute (WIA) on Saturday to celebrate its Annual Survivors’ Reunion Day. The Cancer Institute, which was once a small hospital with no more than 12 beds, is now a testament to numerous stories of survival.The event, organised after a long break due to Covid, brought together survivors of different ages, doctors, nurses and hospital staff.As Diya Fathima went on stage, nurses in the crowd recognised her instantly as the 10-year-old child who was once admitted here. “I was admitted here in 2010. Now I’m in my final year of college,” she said, adding that the hospital gave her a new lease of life.Dr Kalpana Balakrishnan, CEO and medical director of the Cancer Institute, said this event celebrates survivors who recovered and reintegrated into society. She recalled that Dr Muthulakshmi Reddy first envisioned such an institution in 1927 and, after decades of effort, established the Cancer Institute in 1954.Sara Cherian, a cancer survivor, said: “This event reminds you that you’re not alone. ,” she said. She is also the founder of Cherian Foundation, which provides free wigs to the hospital. Deepa Ramani, a-35-year old childhood brain tumour survivor, recalled the emotional struggle of losing her hair during radiation therapy. “We don’t want sympathy but empathy,” she said.
Article Summary: Hundreds of cancer survivors gathered at Adyar Cancer Institute (WIA) on Saturday to celebrate its Annual Survivors’ Reunion Day. The Cancer Institute, which was once a small hospital with no more than 12 beds, is now a testament to numerous stories of survival.

Article Title: Four Coimbatore residents get silver gifts for implementing four-bin source segregation system
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Coimbatore corporation rewarded four residents of ward 38 with silver gifts for implementing the four-bin source segregation system. The newly introduced Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) Management Rules 2026 mandate segregation of waste into four categories — wet, dry, sanitary, and special wastes. Interestingly, west zone has appeared to be the forerunner in implementing the rules.The Union govt has allowed three years for complete compliance of the 2026 rules in all local bodies in the country. The new MSW rules came into effect in May.The rewarded residents were from Anbu Nagar, Sindhu Street and Viruksha street of ward 38. On Friday, corporation commissioner Katta Ravi Teja presented the residents with certificates of appreciation along with the rewards.According to the sanitary officer of the west zone, the residents across the corporation were given awareness of the new MSW rules and in a few days, a couple of residents volunteered to implement the four-bin source segregation system without anyone insisting. The officer said, “Already people are used to giving sanitary waste separately. So, following the new rules would be much easier.”City health officer Dr V C Subash Gandhi said, “No other zone has so far come forward to implement this. Since they have done it out of their own interest, we wanted to appreciate them. The silver gifts for the four residents were sponsored by one of the residents. Residents of the Periyar Nagar in ward 36 have expressed interest to implement the same. So, the corporation has planned to rope in corporate social responsibility funds to buy four bins to 32 houses in that street. We have also planned to engage residents’ welfare associations to implement and reward the best team.”
Article Summary: Coimbatore corporation rewarded four residents of ward 38 with silver gifts for implementing the four-bin source segregation system. The newly introduced Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) Management Rules 2026 mandate segregation of waste into four categories. The Union govt has allowed three years for complete compliance of the 2026 rules in all local bodies in the country.

Article Title: Erode woman burnt alive by man whom she befriended in social media
Article Text:
Representative image





ERODE: A 24-year-old woman was burnt alive in Erode on Wednesday by a man whom she had befriended on a social media platform.The deceased woman has been identified as S Vinodhini, who had been staying with her mother in Bharathi Nagar here after separating from her husband. She developed a friendship with Naveen alias Navaneethakrishnan, 26, of Sayalkudi in Ramanathapuram district.The Erode taluk police said the two had been in regular contact over the phone for several months. “On Wednesday, Naveen visited Vinodhini’s residence and confronted her over what he claimed was her reduced communication with him,” said a police officer. When the argument escalated, Naveen poured kerosene on Vinodhini and set her on fire. The man, who also suffered burn injuries, managed to flee the scene.Neighbours rushed Vinodhini to Erode Government Hospital where she succumbed to the severe burn injuries she had suffered.Meanwhile, Naveen got himself admitted to Amaravathi Government Hospital in Karur district.The Erode taluk police, who registered a case, had passed on information to their counterparts in neighbouring districts about the chances of the murder suspect, who suffered burn injuries, approaching a hospital. The Karur police, who came to know about Naveen getting admitted to Amaravathi Government Hospital, alerted the Erode taluk police on Thursday. A police team from Erode wet to Karur and arrested him. “He will be brought to Erode after his treatment is over,” the officer said.
Article Summary: S Vinodhini, 24, had been staying with her mother in Bharathi Nagar here after separating from her husband. She developed a friendship with Naveen alias Navaneethakrishnan, 26, of Sayalkudi in Ramanathapuram district.
